newsitem.title: USA: Senate confirms Cuomo to be HUD secretary.
newsitem.headline: Senate confirms Cuomo to be HUD secretary.

text.p: The Senate on Wednesday confirmed Andrew Cuomo to be Secretary of Housing and Urban Development by a 99-0 vote.
Cuomo, 39, the son of former New York Gov. Mario Cuomo, has been an assistant HUD secretary for three years. He replaces Henry Cisneros.

He is the third of Clinton's second-term cabinet nominees to be confirmed, joining Secretary of State Madeleine Albright and Defence Secretary William Cohen, who were approved last week, also by 99-0 votes.

Cuomo, whose wife, Kerry, is a daughter of the late Sen. Robert Kennedy, sought as assistant secretary for community planning and development to help the poor by championing programmes to create jobs and provide work training in depressed areas. He also worked to increase funding for the homeless.

"I commend Mr. Cuomo for his record of public service. He has shown innovation, insight and tireless efforts to serve our cities, suburbs and rural areas," Senate Banking Committee Chairman Alfonse D'Amato, a New York Republican, said before the vote.
But D'Amato said Cuomo faced a difficult job in trying to meet the department's goals of providing housing for poor and low-income families on a limited budget.

Cuomo is said to have vaulted to the top of the list to replace Cisneros on the strength of a recommendation from Vice President Al Gore after Cuomo helped Gore prepare for last year's vice presidential debate against Jack Kemp.

Before coming to Washington, Cuomo practiced law as an assistant district attorney in Manhattan and as a partner in a law firm. He also worked as his father's campaign manager and strategist and a special assistant to the Democratic governor.

In 1986, he founded H.E.L.P., which grew to be the largest private provider of transitional housing for the homeless in the United States. In 1991 he was named to head the New York City Commission on the Homeless, the youngest commission chairman in city history.
